A guided warm-up: tell it about your voice and how much time you have, and it builds a routine and walks you through it, with the
piano playing every pattern a half step higher each time, and the band joining in near the end.

## Set up

```{=html}
<form id="vw-setup" class="vw-setup" onsubmit="return false">
  <label>Your voice
    <select id="vw-voice">
      <option value="bass">Bass</option><option value="baritone">Baritone</option><option value="tenor">Tenor</option>
      <option value="alto">Alto / contralto</option><option value="mezzo" selected>Mezzo-soprano</option><option value="soprano">Soprano</option>
    </select></label>
  <label>Time
    <select id="vw-length"><option value="5">5 minutes</option><option value="10" selected>10 minutes</option><option value="15">15 minutes</option><option value="20">20 minutes</option><option value="30">Long (20 minutes or more)</option></select></label>
  <label>Singing for
    <select id="vw-focus"><option value="general">Anything</option><option value="pop">Pop, rock, musical theatre</option><option value="classical">Classical</option><option value="choir">Choir</option></select></label>
  <label>Style
    <select id="vw-style"><option value="standard" selected>Standard</option><option value="fun">Fun (class: sound effects, tongue twisters, pizza)</option></select></label>
  <label>How the voice feels
    <select id="vw-energy"><option value="gentle">Just woke up / tired</option><option value="normal" selected>Normal</option><option value="perform">Performing soon</option></select></label>
  <label>Pace
    <select id="vw-pace"><option value="slow">Slow</option><option value="medium" selected>Medium</option><option value="brisk">Brisk</option></select></label>
  <label>Range
    <select id="vw-shift"><option value="-3">Lower (3 half steps)</option><option value="-1">A little lower</option><option value="0" selected>As usual</option><option value="1">A little higher</option><option value="3">Higher (3 half steps)</option></select></label>
  <fieldset><legend>Include</legend>
    <label class="vw-check"><input type="checkbox" id="vw-stretch" checked> Stretches</label>
    <label class="vw-check"><input type="checkbox" id="vw-breath" checked> Breathing</label>
    <label class="vw-check"><input type="checkbox" id="vw-band" checked> The band</label>
    <label class="vw-check"><input type="checkbox" id="vw-auto" checked> Go on to the next step by itself</label>
  </fieldset>
  <div class="vw-go"><button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" id="vw-build">Build my warm-up</button>
    <span id="vw-summary" class="vw-summary" aria-live="polite"></span></div>
</form>
```

## How it works

- **Body first, then breath, then voice.** Stretches loosen the neck, shoulders, jaw and ribs, which all pull on the larynx.
  Breathing steps wake up the low, wide breath. The singing starts on hums and lip trills (semi-occluded sounds that are easy on
  the folds) and only then opens onto vowels, wider leaps and the top of the range.
- **The piano** plays the starting chord, then the pattern with you, then moves up a half step. It climbs from the low middle of
  your voice to a comfortable top (not your highest note) and comes back down. Set **Range** if it sits too high or low.
- **The band** plays two short grooves: one to sing a scale over as the key climbs, and a slow one to hum over as a cool-down.
- **Gentle** routines stay lower, shorter and softer; **Performing soon** adds agility and a wider top, and ends ready rather than
  cooled down.

- **Fun** swaps in sound-effect sirens, a countdown shake, tongue twisters (spoken, then sung) and bouncy "pizza" staccatos.
  The English twister avoids r/l, f/p, v/b, z/j and th, which are hard for speakers of Korean and some other languages,
  and there is one in Japanese and one in Korean, so other students get to lead.

::: {.callout-warning}
Stop if anything hurts, tickles or feels tight. Warm-ups should feel easy: if a note strains, let the pattern go by and come back on
the way down. Sip water between steps.
:::
